root_cause.text: In the MPTCP PM ADD_ADDR retransmission timer path, the socket reference was released with `__sock_put()` instead of `sock_put()`, and the timer teardown logic did not account for the last-reference case, causing the socket to remain unfreed or deadlock when `sk_free()` synchronously stopped the same timer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `__sock_put(sk)` to `sock_put(sk)` in `mptcp_pm_add_timer()`, adds `entry->timer_done` to avoid calling `sk_stop_timer_sync()` on a timer that is already finishing, and sets that flag when no reschedule occurs; the commit message explicitly says “If at that moment, it was the last reference being held, the sk would not be freed” and that `sk_free()` would otherwise “waiting indefinitely to finish.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add per-entry timer completion state to `mptcp_pm_add_entry`.
intent_record.what: A new boolean field named `timer_done` was added to `struct mptcp_pm_add_entry` between `retrans_times` and `add_timer`.
intent_record.how: This extends each add-entry instance with state to record whether its timer processing has completed, allowing later code to distinguish completed timer work from pending timer activity.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mptcp_pm_add_timer() to lock the socket before state checks and rearm the timer through a unified timeout path.
intent_record.what: The function `mptcp_pm_add_timer()` changes `timeout` from an uninitialized local to `unsigned int timeout = 0;`, moves `bh_lock_sock(sk);` to before the TCP_CLOSE state check, changes the TCP_CLOSE branch to jump to `out` instead of `exit`, and replaces two direct `sk_reset_timer()` calls with assignments to `timeout` (`HZ / 20` and `TCP_RTO_MAX / 8`) before falling through to `out`.
intent_record.how: The timer callback now always acquires the socket lock before inspecting state, avoiding an unlocked state check. Instead of immediately reprogramming the timer in the middle of the function, it records the desired delay and relies on the common exit path to apply it, which makes the locking and timer rearm flow more consistent and avoids using an uninitialized timeout value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust add-address timer backoff handling to stop scheduling retries after the maximum retransmission count is reached.
intent_record.what: The code no longer calls sk_reset_timer() directly with a shifted timeout expression inside the conditional. Instead, it left-shifts the local variable timeout by entry->retrans_times when retrans_times is below ADD_ADDR_RETRANS_MAX, and sets timeout to 0 in the else branch. The subsequent timer reset call is removed from this hunk.
intent_record.how: This changes how the retransmission delay value is prepared before later use: the timeout is now computed in a separate step and explicitly zeroed once the maximum retransmission count is reached. At runtime, this affects when and whether the add-address timer will be armed, preventing further exponential backoff timing once the retry limit is exceeded.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix timer handling in the MPTCP PM add callback by rescheduling active timeouts and correctly marking completion when no timeout remains.
intent_record.what: The timer callback now checks `timeout` in the `out:` path: if it is nonzero, it calls `sk_reset_timer(sk, timer, jiffies + timeout)`, otherwise it sets `entry->timer_done = true` with a comment explaining this avoids waiting for the timer if `sock_put` triggers `sk_free`. The unlock-and-release sequence also changes from `bh_unlock_sock(sk); __sock_put(sk);` to `bh_unlock_sock(sk); sock_put(sk);`, and the old `exit:` label is removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the callback can now re-arm the timer for another interval when a timeout remains, or mark the timer entry as complete when no further timeout is pending so socket teardown can proceed without waiting. Using `sock_put()` instead of `__sock_put()` changes the reference release path to the regular socket put helper after unlocking.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reset the add-address timer completion state when re-arming the timer to avoid stale timer_done status.
intent_record.what: A new assignment `add_entry->timer_done = false;` was inserted at the `reset_timer:` label in `mptcp_pm_alloc_anno_list()` immediately before computing the timeout and arming `add_entry->add_timer`.
intent_record.how: Each time this code path resets or reuses the add-address timer, it now explicitly clears the `timer_done` state first, ensuring the entry is treated as not yet completed and preventing stale completion state from affecting subsequent timer handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid stop-syncing timers that have already completed when freeing annotated MPTCP PM entries.
intent_record.what: In the free-loop inside mptcp_pm_free_anno_list(), the unconditional call to sk_stop_timer_sync(sk, &entry->add_timer) was replaced with a conditional call guarded by 'if (!entry->timer_done)'. The kfree_rcu(entry, rcu) call remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now skips stopping the add_timer for entries whose timer has already completed, avoiding an unnecessary or potentially invalid timer stop operation during cleanup. For entries still pending, the timer is stopped as before before the object is freed via RCU.

Author: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>

    mptcp: pm: ADD_ADDR rtx: always decrease sk refcount

The diff also removes the earlier `if (!msk) return;` early return. This indicates the bug was present before and the shown code already contains the fix for the leak/deadlock by ensuring the reference is released in all cases.

This matches the commit message’s stated fix for the timer callback data-race.
